definitionBean.title: Chemical Equation
definitionBean.definition: Representing a chemical reaction in a concise form using symbols and chemical formulas is called a 'chemical equation'.
definitionBean.explanation: Using chemical symbols and formulas of substances instead of words makes equations more concise and useful. Reactants are written on the left and products on the right.
importantPoints: Use of symbols for reactants and products
Balancing the equation to obey the law of conservation of mass

questions.text: Quick Revision - Word Equation and Chemical Formula

definitionBean.title: Word Equation and Chemical Formula
definitionBean.definition: When a chemical reaction is written using the names (words) of substances, it is a word equation, and representing it through chemical formulas is a chemical formula.
definitionBean.explanation: A word equation is the initial stage of understanding a reaction. Chemical formulas denote the composition of a compound using the symbols of its elements.
importantPoints: Word equation: Writing names of reactants and products
Chemical formula: Notations based on symbols and valencies of elements
Symbolic representation is more scientific and concise

questions.text: Quick Revision - Writing Chemical Equations and State Symbols

definitionBean.title: Writing Chemical Equations and State Symbols
definitionBean.definition: To make a chemical equation more informative, physical state symbols are written alongside the reactants and products.
definitionBean.explanation: Symbols like (s) for solid, (l) for liquid, (g) for gas, and (aq) for aqueous solution are used.

questions.text: Subject: Chemical Equation and Word Equation

parts.statement: What is a chemical equation? Why is it more useful than a word equation?
parts.correct_answer: A chemical equation is a concise representation using symbols and formulas that is more informative.
parts.explanation: A chemical equation is a concise representation of a chemical reaction using symbols and formulas. It is more useful than a word equation because it saves space, is universally understood, and reveals the exact quantities or numbers of reactants and products.

parts.statement: What is a word equation? Explain with an example.
parts.correct_answer: An equation expressed in words is called a word equation.
parts.explanation: When a chemical reaction is expressed in terms of the names of the substances participating in it, it is called a word equation. For example: Zinc + Sulfuric acid $\rightarrow$ Zinc sulfate + Hydrogen.

questions.text: Subject: Writing Chemical Equations and Formulas

parts.statement: What are the main steps in writing a chemical equation? Write briefly.
parts.correct_answer: Writing reactants and products on left and right using formulas and an arrow.
parts.explanation: Steps for writing a chemical equation: 1. Write reactants on the left side with a (+) sign between them. 2. Write products on the right side with a (+) sign between them. 3. Place an arrow sign ($\rightarrow$) between reactants and products to indicate the direction of the reaction.

parts.statement: What is the importance of a chemical formula? Explain.
parts.correct_answer: A chemical formula gives precise information on atom counts and symbols.
parts.explanation: A chemical formula gives precise information about the number of atoms of different elements present in one molecule of a compound and their symbols, making it easier to write and understand chemical equations.

parts.statement: What do the symbols indicating physical states (s, l, g, aq) mean in a chemical equation? Explain with examples.
parts.correct_answer: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, and (aq) aqueous solution.
parts.explanation: To make chemical equations more informative, physical states are added: (s) for solid, (l) for liquid, (g) for gas, and (aq) for aqueous solution. Example: $\text{CaO(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$

parts.statement: If a gas is evolved or a precipitate is formed in a chemical reaction, how is it represented in the equation?
parts.correct_answer: An upward arrow ($\uparrow$) for gas and downward arrow ($\downarrow$) for precipitate are used.
parts.explanation: In case a gas is evolved, an upward arrow ($\uparrow$) or (g) is written next to the formula of the gas, and if a precipitate is formed, a downward arrow ($\downarrow$) or (s) is written.
